name: Materials Science

papers.title: On the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on low-index Au surfaces
papers.abstract: Many multi-phase thin films grown by self-assembly involve co-deposition of both metallic and oxide phases that grow into the same film. Under such conditions, the oxide species may be present in stoichiometric molecular form on the surface of the metallic phase. Quantifying the stability, binding, and diffusion of such molecular oxide states on metallic surfaces is critical for understanding self-assembly. In this work, we investigate the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on Au surfaces using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. Specifically, we examine how the configuration of the CeO2 molecule, its binding energy and binding free energy, structural stability, effective charge, and projected electronic density of states vary among various binding sites on Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) surfaces. Molecular CeO2 was found to be more favorable on all Au surfaces than its atomic constituents. It was also found that the bent CeO2 molecule configuration is more stable than the linear counterpart, with the Ce atom on the hollow site and the O atoms on the top sites. In addition, the configurations of the CeO2 molecule on Au surfaces with a binding energy around or weaker than -1 eV were found to have a low probability of existence above room temperature. Furthermore, the charge transfer was found to occur in such a way that the CeO2 molecule becomes polarized on all surfaces, but the polarization is stronger only for the strongly bonded states on Au(001) and Au(110) surfaces. Finally, three different cases of how the CeO2 molecule binds to Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) were identified: case 1: chemisorption with symmetric bonds, case 2: chemisorption with asymmetric bonds, and case 3: physisorption with symmetric bonds. These three cases of CeO2 binding are present on Au(001) and Au(110), but only cases 2 and 3 occur on Au(111).

papers.title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics
papers.abstract: Stretchable, skin-conformal electronics demand thermal interface materials that combine high through-plane heat transport with mechanical softness and lateral electrical insulation. In particle-filled composites, these requirements are typically antagonistic. Heat transport is governed not only by the intrinsic thermal conductivity of the fillers but, more critically, by thermal resistance at the interparticle interface. As the interparticle distance is reduced by increasing the particle content, mechanical reinforcement and in-plane electrical conductivity become unavoidable. The existing particle alignment processing strategies result in inefficient uncoupling of multifunctionality. Here, we present a hierarchical two-step process strategy to induce strong conductivity anisotropy in a soft composite. First, an align-before-blend process forms a scaffold of magnetically aligned nickel (Ni) microparticles in air before polymer infiltration. The absence of the viscous elastomer matrix during the particle alignment facilitates handling large amounts of particles, which assemble into highly ordered and densely packed vertical heat-conduction pathways. Second, a liquid metal (LM)/Ni mixture is infiltrated into the aligned scaffold to bridge interparticle gaps, minimizing interparticle thermal resistance. The composite reaches 7.5 W/(m K) through-plane thermal conductivity with lateral electrical conductivity below $10^{-12}$ S/m and ultrasoft mechanical compliance (approximately 160 kPa), enabling coupling layers in thermoelectric generators and finger-mounted heat-spreading pads for wearable technologies.

papers.title: Unveiling ferroelectricity in wafer-scale beta-phase In$_2$Se$_3$
papers.abstract: Pushing ferroelectricity to the ultimate thickness limit is a central challenge for memory hardware, because conventional three-dimensional ferroelectrics degrade through depolarization and interfacial effects when thinned. Here we identify $\beta$-In$_2$Se$_3$, a van der Waals semiconductor regarded as centrosymmetric, as a host of bistable polar order arising from a picometre-scale distortion within each quintuple layer. The polar state has out-of-plane and in-plane components, is switched by a vertical electric field, and persists to the bilayer limit (~1.9 nm) with an estimated coercive field of 0.9 MV/cm and an apparent remanent polarization of 11.0 $\mu$C/cm$^2$. Films grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on 2-inch wafers yield capacitor arrays with a switching-voltage spread below 5% across 100 devices, an endurance of $10^7$ cycles and a projected ten-year retention. Because the polar state coexists with a semiconducting gap, one film serves as both the switching layer of a capacitor and the channel of a ferroelectric semiconductor transistor.

papers.title: Electron--phonon interactions in a pseudo--atomic orbital basis: superconductivity, transport, spectroscopy and thermal emission from one interpolated vertex
papers.abstract: Electron--phonon interactions govern superconductivity, electrical resistivity, optical absorption and electronic excitation lifetimes in solids. First--principles calculations require interpolating this coupling onto dense Brillouin--zone grids, traditionally using maximally localized Wannier functions that demand material--specific tuning. Here we show that a fixed basis of pseudo--atomic orbitals--automatically generated from pseudopotentials and implemented in the open--source code PAOFLOW captures the electron--phonon vertex with equivalent accuracy and no manual tuning. Computed from density--functional perturbation theory or displaced supercells, and incorporating long--range fields and spin--orbit coupling, the vertex matches established codes on identical inputs. We validate the method on lead, reproducing its phonon dispersion, superconducting gap, critical temperature, resistivity, photoemission kink and cyclotron masses, and on silicon, capturing phonon--assisted optical absorption, wafer emissivity and carrier mobilities. This parameter--free framework enables high--throughput, automated electron--phonon calculations across large materials databases.

papers.title: Low-barrier-height Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ ferroelectric tunnel junctions with large ON-state currents
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) hold great promise for nonvolatile memory, neuromorphic computing, and other applications. Hf$_\text{1-x}$Zr$_\text{x}$O$_2$ (HZO) has become a leading candidate for the tunnel barrier due primarily to its compatibility with CMOS technology. Recent advances on HZO based FTJs have highlighted the importance of understanding the electrical transport through a ferroelectric tunnel barrier for fulfilling the technological promises of FTJs. In this paper we report investigation of HZO FTJs featuring a barrier of ultrathin HZO ($\leq$5nm) measured down to a temperature of 2 K. Direct quantum tunneling was found to dominate at low temperatures, along with contributions from trap-assisted tunneling. As the temperature increases, conduction by thermal activation takes over. We developed a minimal model that accounts for all experimental observations, revealing a barrier height significantly lower than that of the band alignment picture, an unexpected finding attributable to the emergence of a shallow trap band. This finding reveals a previously unexplored pathway toward simultaneously achieving large ON-state currents, high tunnel electroresistance and improved temperature stability for the high-speed memory applications of FTJs.

papers.title: ILMlip: fast and universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: Large-scale pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials keep growing more accurate as new models appear at a rapid pace, and more expensive: the current leader of Matbench Discovery as of November 2026 (F1 score 0.935) has $9.9\times10^7$ parameters and took 3.6 thousand GPU-hours to train. The ILMlip potentials presented here are optimised for speed as well as zero-shot accuracy. They are equivariant, conservative message-passing potentials in which every component is arranged for throughput: little work per pair of atoms and as much as needed per atom. Through ASE on one GPU, they run molecular dynamics up to about $10^3$ times faster than state-of-the-art message-passing potentials such as MACE (medium) and up to five times faster than NEP89 and DPA-4.1C. At the same time, six sizes with $1.4\times10^5$ to $2.8\times10^7$ parameters, pretrained on materials, molecules and solid acids, reach F1 scores of 0.75 to 0.91 on Matbench Discovery, placing the largest within 0.03 of the current leader. They therefore suit high-throughput, large or long simulations, and, being transferable, they are strong starting points for fine-tuning. Fine-tuned to six materials, the model of size S comes close to the ab initio force errors of a fine-tuned MACE, so it reaches reference-level accuracy at about 50 ns per atom and step (Cu fcc). Their components can be adopted separately, as a starting point for architectures with even better ratios of speed to accuracy. The ILMlip implementation is available at https://github.com/jhaens/ilmlip

papers.title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-\delta}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) offer efficient energy conversion at intermediate temperatures, but their performance is often constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics at the cathode. Triple conducting perovskite materials such as BaCo$_x$Fe$_y$Zr$_z$Y$_{1-x-y-z}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZY) have shown promise as air electrodes. In this study, we investigated the impact of Y doping on proton conductivity by decoupling the effects on proton diffusivity and proton concentration. Using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we assessed proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions: BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.2}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZ), BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.1}$Y$_{0.1}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZY0.1) and BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Y$_{0.2}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFY). Thermodynamic defect models incorporating hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation reactions are employed to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations. Our results suggest that increasing the Y content from BCFZ to BCFY increases proton diffusivity by 1.7% at 500 $^\circ$C. Under PCFC operating gas conditions, proton concentration and proton conductivity are predicted to increase by 3.8% and 5.3%, respectively, at 500 $^\circ$C. These increases are modest compared with the larger enhancements reported experimentally under reducing conditions, highlighting the importance of gas conditions in evaluating the effects of Y doping. Under low oxygen partial pressure conditions, we predict that the dominant proton transport mechanism shifts from hydroxyl groups (OH$_O^{\bullet}$) to hydride species (H$_O^{\bullet}$). This work provides mechanistic insight into proton transport in BCFZY cathodes and offers design principles for optimizing proton-conducting air electrodes in next-generation PCFCs.

papers.title: Machine-Learning Spin-Fermion Models for Strongly Disordered Magnets: Sb-Doped MnTe
papers.abstract: Metallic altermagnets are promising for spintronics, but most altermagnets are insulating. Doping can induce metallicity, but introduces chemical and magnetic disorder that is challenging to model from first principles. Here, we introduce a machine-learning approach that renormalizes first-principles calculations onto disordered spin-fermion models. The learned models accurately reproduce first-principles magnetic and electronic properties and enable predictions of millions of inequivalent long-range exchange couplings in large disordered supercells. Applied to Sb-doped MnTe, the approach shows that altermagnetism persists up to about 25\% Sb, and reveals disorder broadening as a new factor controlling spin selectivity. More broadly, our work opens a route to combining renormalization with machine-learned Hamiltonians for strongly disordered materials.

papers.title: Electron exchange matters in electron spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) conventionally considers classical Coulomb interactions between probe and material electrons, overlooking their fermionic exchange at relativistic energies. Here, we develop a relativistic theory of magnon EELS incorporating both magnetic dipole and electron exchange interactions. We show that the two channels leave distinguishable electron spin states, suppressing their interference in conventional EELS. However, spin-resolved detection erases this which-path information, revealing first-order interference despite the weak exchange amplitude. Remarkably, the same interference produces a left-right intensity asymmetry with a spin-polarized incident beam, without requiring outgoing-spin analysis. We demonstrate that this signal directly probes magnon angular momentum and distinguishes excitations of opposite handedness, opening a route to nanoscale measurements of chiral magnetic excitations.

papers.title: Solvent-Mediated Disintegration of a Vitrimer Network
papers.abstract: Vitrimers are dynamic polymer networks characterized by associative bond exchange, which enables topological rearrangement while preserving the overall network connectivity. However, how this dynamic connectivity evolves in the presence of a solvent, particularly as a function of temperature, remains poorly understood. Here, we employ hybrid molecular dynamics Monte Carlo simulations to elucidate the temperature-dependent restructuring and dissociation of vitrimer networks in solution. By constructing temperature composition phase diagrams, we demonstrate that the critical temperature for network dissolution increases nonlinearly with crosslink concentration. We find that the network disintegration begins well below the critical dissolution temperature, indicating that the loss of network connectivity can occur even before the onset of macroscopic dissolution. However, the network undergoes extensive restructuring around the critical temperature for a highly crosslinked system, resulting in the formation of numerous smaller, disconnected networks. Concurrently, the number of intrachain dynamic bonds increases with temperature. Interestingly, complete disintegration into individual polymer chains is not observed; instead, the solution comprises a broad distribution of smaller network fragments. These findings reveal the complex interplay between solvent-induced network disintegration and dynamic bond redistribution, providing molecular level insights into the dissolution of vitrimer networks and their potential for solvent assisted recycling.

papers.title: Exact subtraction of electron self-interaction from the Kohn-Sham equations
papers.abstract: The self-interaction error (SIE) of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) leads to a non-physical, non-linear dependence of an orbital's energy on its own fractional occupation [Dabo et al., Phys. Rev. B, 82:115121, 2010]. The generalized Koopmans condition (GKC) ensures an atomic orbital's eigenenergy is independent of its fractional occupation$-$ and is free of self-interaction. The constrained search of the Levy spin-density-functional theory yields orbital densities and delivers the ground-state energy to generalize the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems. In this work, the electron density of the Kohn-Sham equations is constrained to be orbital-density dependent, with a total energy functional linear with respect to variation of its orbital densities. That is, the KS multiplicative effective potential $v_{\text{s}}[{n}]$ for an orbital $\varphi_i[{n}]$ is constrained to a functional $v_{\text{eff}}[{n - n_i}]$. The result complies with the generalized Koopmans condition (GKC). This approach improves LDA and GGA mean absolute errors (MAEs) in fundamental band gaps by $\sim$ 1 eV, with respect to KS-DFT. Equations free of electron self-interaction provide the basis for improvements in the accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity of density functional theories.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Triangular Sc-rich Nanodomains: The Orign of Anomalous Alloy Scattering in ScAlN/GaN Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Wurtzite scandium aluminium nitride (ScAlN) alloys hold substantial potential for GaN heterostructure high-electron mobility transistors, owing to their large spontaneous polarization gradient and the ability to achieve precise lattice matching at heterointerface. Nevertheless, despite continuous advances in epitaxy and device fabrication, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) mobility in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures remains persistently limited, and the underlying microscopic origin remains elusive. Here, we uncover an anomalous electron scattering mechanism from laterally correlated alloy disorder that spontaneously develops within the ScAlN barrier driven by strain-field undulations imposed by threading dislocations. Dislocation strain field partitions the growth front into nanoscale domains with distinct strain states, driving anisotropic diffusion of Sc adatoms and yielding crystallographically oriented triangular Sc-rich nanodomains. Reducing the threading dislocation density from 2.8E10 to 4.4E8 cm^-2 suppresses areal density of nanodomains by more than two orders of magnitude. As a result, low-temperature Hall mobility increases from 1800 to 11995 cm^2*V^-1*s^-1. These findings establish dislocation-mediated Sc-rich nanodomains as the dominant source of anomalously strong alloy scattering, resolving the mobility bottleneck for high-performance nitride electronics.

papers.title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
papers.abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

papers.title: Phono3GPU: GPU-Accelerated Linear Tetrahedron Integration for Phonon Thermal Transport
papers.abstract: Materials with high or low thermal conductivity are increasingly important for thermal management and energy technologies. Machine-learned interatomic potentials have accelerated anharmonic force-constant calculations, shifting the bottleneck toward phonon transport calculations for large materials datasets. Existing GPU solvers often rely on smearing, whose width can require material-dependent choices, while the linear tetrahedron method used in phono3py avoids this parameter but becomes costly for complex structures. Here we introduce Phono3GPU, which reformulates three-phonon scattering and linear tetrahedron integration for massively parallel GPU execution. Across benchmark crystals, Phono3GPU accelerates total calculations by up to 41 times relative to a CPU implementation, with larger gains for complex unit cells, and by 2 to 6 times relative to a recent GPU plug-in for phono3py. We further demonstrate atom-resolved scattering analysis in defective silicon supercells as an application enabled by the reduced computational cost. Phono3GPU thus lowers the cost of tetrahedron-based thermal-conductivity calculations and of detailed investigations of structure-dependent phonon transport.

papers.title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

papers.title: Revisiting the Schottky-Mott Relation for Metal/ Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Interfaces: The Role of Interface Dipoles
papers.abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. Our findings indicate that FLP is intrinsically governed by both long-range dipole interactions and extended short-range Lennard-Jones potentials. This framework, in conjunction with the linear Schottky-Mott relation, improves predictive capabilities in contact engineering.

papers.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
papers.abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 \AA$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 \AA$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

papers.title: Quantum Geometric Origin of Néel-Order-Driven Magneto-Optical Response in MnTe
papers.abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the N\'{e}el order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic N\'{e}el-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the N\'{e}el-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ N\'{e}el-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated N\'{e}el order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between N\'{e}el order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of N\'{e}el order in altermagnetic MnTe.

papers.title: Quantum Metric Connects Bond Delocalization to Phonon Softening
papers.abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
papers.abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

papers.title: Anisotropic magnetic-field modulation of hysteretic sheet resistance in few-layer ferroelectric WTe2
papers.abstract: Ferroelectricity in few-layer WTe2, a polar semimetal, originates from interlayer sliding and can be probed through gate-dependent resistance hysteresis. Yet the role of magnetic fields in this transport signature remains largely unexplored. Here, we examine magnetic-field-induced changes in the hysteresis in exfoliated few-layer WTe2. Applying an out-of-plane magnetic field produces a pronounced hysteresis enhancement, while an in-plane field yields a negligible response. Analysis of the individual hysteresis branches reveals distinct magnetotransport responses of the two ferroelectric states, which increase their resistance separation under magnetic field. The enhancement exhibits a robust power-law field dependence and a temperature evolution closely resembling that of magnetoresistance. Our results reveal a close association between anisotropic magnetotransport and ferroelectric hysteresis, underscoring the interplay between magnetic response and ferroic order in a two-dimensional polar semimetal.

papers.title: Magnetization, susceptibility, and entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped homometallic tetranuclear and pentanuclear Cu(II) complexes
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical investigation of the magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and quantum entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped tetranuclear ($Cu_4$) and pentanuclear ($Cu_5$) Cu(II) clusters, motivated by experimentally realized molecular spin systems. In both cases, the study presents a discussion of the comparison between experimental data and theoretical analytical calculations of magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature. The correlation between magnetization jumps and magnetic susceptibility peaks, along with the presence of entanglement entropy plateaus as a function of external magnetic fields, is analyzed in the low-temperature regime. Overall, the results demonstrate that the cluster size, geometry, and interaction anisotropy play a crucial role in shaping both the thermodynamic and the entanglement properties. In addition, the study is based on antiferromagnetic Heisenberg spin Hamiltonians, with the inclusion of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

papers.title: Electronic topological modes in hexagonal NbSi$_{2}$ with a double helix
papers.abstract: Chiral systems can host nontrivial topological states, including characteristic edge modes and Fermi arcs. Here, we investigate the electronic properties of hexagonal NbSi$_2$ with chiral symmetry using first-principles calculations for both bulk and slab geometries. We find that spin--orbit coupling (SOC) is relatively weak. Notably, the topological edge state originates from structural chirality rather than the SOC. From the Berry curvature analysis, we confirm the existence of Weyl points, some of which carry a Chern number of $\pm 2$. Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of chiral edge modes with extended Fermi arcs around high-symmetry points. Finally, we investigate the real-space localization using spatially resolved and site-dependent density of states (DOS). We demonstrate that the surface states can be exclusively associated with the chiral Si chains.

papers.title: LetzElPhC: an electron-phonon code for efficient exciton-phonon workflows
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{LetzElPhC}, an open-source software package that computes electron-phonon matrix elements from the output of density functional perturbation theory calculations performed with the \texttt{Quantum ESPRESSO} code. By interfacing directly with the \texttt{Yambo} code and exploiting crystal symmetries, \texttt{LetzElPhC} enables a scalable workflow for evaluating exciton-phonon matrix elements while enforcing strict gauge consistency between one-electron Bloch states and Bethe-Salpeter excitonic wave functions across the full Brillouin zone. This symmetry-preserving approach avoids phase ambiguities and significantly reduces both computational costs and memory requirements. To support large-scale simulations on dense momentum grids, the package incorporates Fourier interpolation of dynamical matrices and perturbed Kohn-Sham potentials, accounting for long-range dipole and quadrupole interactions in both two- and three-dimensional materials, combined with multi-level parallelization and efficient parallel I/O. Together, these capabilities seamlessly complement the \texttt{Yambo} code to enable first-principles simulations of phonon-assisted optical spectroscopies, which we demonstrate through applications to resonant Raman scattering in monolayer $\text{WSe}_2$ and phonon-assisted luminescence in cubic AgBr.

papers.title: AFM metrology for 3D high aspect ratio semiconductor structures
papers.abstract: Transistors have long been the foundation of the semiconductor industry, with continuous architectural innovations enabling the scaling of integrated circuits while maintaining high performance. Advancements in deposition and lithographic techniques have further expanded design possibilities, while increasing structural complexity demands stricter process control. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) offers a rapid and reliable metrology solution, providing high-resolution measurements and robust statistical analysis of critical parameters. In this work, we present clearly resolved individual profiles of lines and spaces in high aspect ratio (HAR) gate all around FET (GAAFET)-type structures on both the nanosheet (NS) region and in the isolation region between the nanosheets and we present a comprehensive statistical evaluation of their critical dimensions.

papers.title: Magnetic Reconfiguration Controls Spin Splitting and Spin-Orbit-Coupled Responses in Compensated Magnets
papers.abstract: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8. Our results establish magnetic reconfiguration as a powerful symmetry-guided strategy for dramatically reshaping electronic and transport responses in compensated magnets.

papers.title: High-Throughput Orientation Extraction via Symmetry-Adapted Filters
papers.abstract: An algorithm for finding the orientation of objects in an image that have a known rotational symmetry, the symmetry-adapted filter (SAF) algorithm, is presented. It is deterministic and training-free, which makes it fast and reproducible. A filter that encodes the known rotational symmetry and approximate peak width is centered on the symmetry center of the object of interest, masked to the region of interest, and rotated to maximize its inner product with the image. The approach is demonstrated on more than 20,000 small-angle neutron scattering images of a torque-driven skyrmion lattice. It is also demonstrated on atomically resolved real-space images, where mapping local atomic orientations enabled the identification of grains and grain boundaries and the quantification of lattice relaxation.

papers.title: EGQCA Code: automated high-throughput thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions
papers.abstract: Modeling disordered systems from first principles across the full composition range is a long-standing computational challenge. We present a code package implementing the extended generalized quasichemical approximation (EGQCA), which describes solid solutions through the statistics of a finite set of clusters and enables their thermodynamic modeling at arbitrary compositions and temperatures. The package automates the complete workflow and interfaces with both DFT codes and universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). We show that replacing DFT with uMLIPs reduces the cost of the cluster calculations by up to five orders of magnitude while preserving the thermodynamic predictions. To make computationally demanding properties tractable, we additionally introduce a cluster-selection algorithm that identifies the most relevant configurations. Together, these developments establish EGQCA as a fast and accurate framework for the thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions and a practical route toward high-throughput screening of disordered materials.

papers.title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $\gamma$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: The region of fcc stability in Fe-rich Fe-Cr alloys, the $\gamma$-loop, has an anomalous shape: at low temperatures, Cr addition initially stabilizes fcc, but above 8 at.% Cr it stabilizes bcc. At high temperatures, Cr always stabilizes bcc. This behavior reflects a delicate balance between magnetic, vibrational and configurational free-energy contributions that is challenging to capture from first principles. We investigate phase stability in Fe1-xCrx (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) using coupled atomistic spin dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration. Gibbs free energy differences between fcc and bcc are calculated from 800 to 1800 K. Our calculations reproduce the experimental $\gamma$-loop and its compositional dependence, with near-quantitative accuracy for the $\gamma$-$\delta$ transition. The $\alpha$-$\gamma$ boundary, including its anomalous shape, is reproduced qualitatively, although transition temperatures are underestimated by approximately 200 K. Static calculations of magnetically ordered and disordered states provide an explanation: in ordered states, increasing Cr initially reduces the energetic preference for bcc over fcc, whereas in disordered states, Cr progressively stabilizes bcc at all compositions. Vibrational effects contribute to phase stability, while atomic short-range clustering at higher Cr content ($x \geq 0.15$) may explain the observed closing of the $\gamma$-loop from below. The simulations reveal finite Cr moments in the paramagnetic state, whose magnitudes depend on their local magnetic environment. The results demonstrate that the anomalous $\gamma$-loop arises from the interplay of magnetic energetics, magnetic disorder, lattice vibrations and chemical clustering, which must be treated on equal footing to capture phase stability from first principle

papers.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense $\mathbf{q}$-Grids Using Set Covers
papers.abstract: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force. This approach unfortunately typically suffers from requiring very large supercells, even for modest $\mathbf{q}$-grids. The non-diagonal supercell method remedies this issue by determining the smallest supercell commensurate with a given $\mathbf{q}$-point, drastically reducing the supercell size, but in turn requiring a new supercell for each $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid. This introduces redundancy, however, since a single non-diagonal supercell may be commensurate with several $\mathbf{q}$-points. In this work I present a method to determine a minimal set of supercells, such that every $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid is commensurate with at least one supercell. I present an algorithm to solve the problem and prove that it yields the optimal solution, before summarizing the algorithm using pseudocode. The scaling of the number of supercells with the density of the grid is discussed. Numerical results on a variety of systems show the significant computational advantage of the method, which increases with the density of the grid.

papers.title: Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
papers.abstract: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave. There, the broken rotational symmetry about the interface normal exerts an orbital torque, and the accumulated angular impulse---the product of the torque and the dwell time---leads to a transverse spatial shift. Applying this mechanism to altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling, we show that the orbital torque is odd in spin. As a consequence, the two spin channels are deflected to opposite sides of the incident plane, giving an intrinsic spatial spin separation in altermagnets. The shift also inherits the angular symmetry of the altermagnetic spin splitting and is strongly enhanced near the onset of total reflection. Our work thus uncovers a new mechanism for transverse shifts, predicts a novel spin separation effect in altermagnets, and offers a direct probe of the altermagnetic order.

papers.title: Measuring a buried Bi$_2$Te$_3$ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
papers.abstract: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--P\'erot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi$_2$Te$_3$ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

papers.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
papers.abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice
papers.abstract: We establish a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice with interaction potential $\phi(t)=(1-e^{-3t^2})/6$ and an antiplane crack far field $K\sqrt{r}\sin(\theta/2)$. We construct a connected branch of equilibria whose single-cell segment contains exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds, with a stability sequence of stable, Morse index one, and stable in the full energy space. The fold loads satisfy $0.45897<K_-<0.45923$ and $0.46219<K_+<0.46242$, establishing a strictly positive lattice-trapping width $K_+-K_->0.00296$. A uniqueness argument establishes exact translation closure and smooth continuation across lattice cells. The proof combines renormalized energy, Schur complement estimates, analytic infinite-tail bounds, interval arithmetic, and exact integer positivity certificates. All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

papers.title: Large-deformation constitutive modeling of viscoelastic foams: Application to an open-cell foam material
papers.abstract: Open-cell elastomeric foams are widely utilized for impact protection and cushioning applications. These foams can demonstrate remarkable elastic compressibility and rate sensitivity over a wide range of force and acceleration protection levels. They often exhibit volumetric-distortional coupling in their mechanical response and potentially compaction banding when subjected to dynamic loads. Here, a phenomenological modeling framework, adopted previously for closed-cell foams, is specified using an experimental characterization-based approach for calibrating and validating the large-deformation, viscoelastic material model. Homogeneous simple compression and tension experiments were performed on isotropic, open-cell viscoelastic foam materials, and stress-strain and lateral-axial strain data were used for model calibration. Data were collected at decadal strain rates to inform the rate-sensitive aspects of the model. The modeling approach involved decomposing the total material response into an equilibrium hyperelastic contribution and several nonlinear, Maxwell-like contributions and utilized invariants of the logarithmic strain to account for large deformations and the strong volumetric-distortional coupling effect. A new strain localization detection algorithm was developed and used to check for the formation of compaction bands, which would invalidate modeling assumptions for the calibration experiments. To validate the predictive capability of the constitutive model, experiments were conducted that involved intentionally inhomogeneous deformations over a spectrum of strain rates and deformation types. The consistency between the measured responses from the validation experiments and the model predictions obtained from finite-element-based numerical simulations was largely within the experimental uncertainty bounds, demonstrating the predictive capability of the model.

papers.title: Geometry Sets the Neutral MLIP-DFT Gap in Non-Covalent Binding, and Charged Systems Fail
papers.abstract: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are widely expected to substitute for explicit quantum chemistry when screening molecular interactions. On non-covalent binding we find that this expectation holds for neutral chemistry and fails for charged chemistry. We audit the FAIRChem UMA OMol head, without task-specific fine-tuning, on 5,567 probe-target dimers from 18 benchmarks across nine fidelity arms, using RAPIDS (Rapid Atomistic Probe-target Interaction Discovery Scaffold), a training-free inference-time scaffold. First, on neutral chemistry RAPIDS reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.37 kcal/mol, matching or beating every explicit DFT single-point fidelity (1.42-1.50 kcal/mol), so the remaining MLIP-DFT gap is geometric rather than a learned-surface error. Second, charged systems form a qualitatively different regime: MAE jumps to 8.5-22.9 kcal/mol across three charged benchmarks; DFT single-point rescoring does not restore accuracy, geometry reoptimization restores it for ionic hydrogen bonds and ion-molecule dimers, and the failure persists across all three MLIP backbones. Third, the residual failures are structured: signed biases cluster by chemistry family, and whether a fidelity fails catastrophically transfers across families more reliably than error magnitude, enabling cost-aware fidelity selection. RAPIDS-Select, a closed-form rule on cheap precomputed features, uses about 37% less compute than a strong static DFT baseline at matched accuracy, and on a newly computed charged benchmark cuts the catastrophe rate from 68% to 5.7%. On WetSenseBench, a wet-lab-grounded host-guest selectivity benchmark from eight sensing studies, RAPIDS without DFT follow-up recovers 82.9% pair-level agreement on the seven studies above its ~1 kcal/mol precision floor.

papers.title: Structural Anisotropy in Bi$_2$Se$_3$/$\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ Topological Insulator/Superconductor Bilayer
papers.abstract: We investigate the crystallographic-orientation dependence of the response of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ ($\lambda$-Ga) to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition. Cross-sectional focused-ion-beam (FIB) imaging confirms formation of a deposited Bi$_2$Se$_3$-containing layer and a distinct interface with $\lambda$-Ga. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD) shows that the coated $\lambda$-Ga crystal remains structurally intact but exhibits a strongly orientation-dependent, non-monotonic response, with the largest modification for the $ab$-plane after 4 min of deposition, whereas the $ac$-plane remains comparatively unchanged. This condition corresponds to the intermediate-deposition regime previously identified at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ thickness of approximately 110 nm. First-principles calculations based on the refined structures show the largest orientation-dependent electronic modification under the same conditions. Complementary optical spectroscopy of Bi$_2$Se$_3$/SiO$_2$ films shows deposition-time-dependent evolution of the film response. These results establish a pronounced crystallographic anisotropy in the structural and calculated electronic response of $\lambda$-Ga to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition.

papers.title: Transport Layer-Driven Optimization of Color and Efficiency in TADF OLEDs for Large-Area Applications
papers.abstract: Balancing structural simplicity with high efficiency is crucial for practical applications of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), especially in large-area lighting devices. Optimizing the charge-transport layers in multilayer OLEDs controls the recombination zone within the emissive layer, thereby enhancing the device's performance. Herein, we experimentally and computationally investigate how the thicknesses of the electron and hole transport layers affect the performance of orange-red thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs. Using a TADF emitter, 2-[4-(diphenylamino)phenyl]-10,10-dioxide-9H-thioxanthen-9-one (TXO-TPA), at 10 wt\% concentration in 4,4-Bis(N-carbazolyl)-1,1-biphenyl (CBP) host, we achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency ($\eta_{EQE}$) of 20.86\% and a peak luminance of 32,800 cd m$^{-2}$. Using a combination of drift-diffusion and optical simulations, we reveal how variations in hole- and electron-transport-layer thicknesses modulate the charge-carrier balance and shift the recombination zone within the emissive layer. This tuning not only optimizes exciton formation but also enables color tuning from green to red without altering the emissive material. Our findings highlight the critical role of transport layer engineering in achieving efficient, color-controlled OLEDs with simplified architectures. Furthermore, we successfully demonstrate a large-area OLED device (~20 cm$^{2}$), achieving an impressive $\eta_{EQE}$ of 17\%, underscoring the scalability and practicality of our approach for general lighting applications.

papers.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
papers.abstract: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

papers.title: Tunable quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect in the PT-symmetric sliding antiferroelectric MoS$_2$
papers.abstract: The quantum metric, the real part of a quantum geometric tensor, plays an important role in fundamental transport and optical responses of quantum materials. While net quantum metric effects are typically realized by breaking both time-reversal (T) and inversion (P) symmetries, valley-contrast mechanisms enable the probing of quantum geometry in centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic systems, revealing physical signatures beyond Berry curvature. Here, we design a four-layer MoS$_2$ platform that combines sliding antiferroelectric order with strain-induced $C_{3z}$ breaking to realize a quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect (NVHE) under preserved P and T symmetries. Reversible interlayer sliding (ABBA $\leftrightarrow$ BAAB) provides nonvolatile electrical control of the valley response. First-principles calculations reveal an outer-layer-dominated NVHE with tunable sign and magnitude. This symmetry-preserving, sliding-tunable strategy activates hidden quantum geometric phenomena in realistic two-dimensional materials and opens a clean pathway for tunable valleytronics and quantum information devices.

papers.title: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents
papers.abstract: Amine-impregnated sorbents with the highest nominal CO2 capacity are frequently the least deployable, as amine beyond the pore-volume limit blocks active sites. Yet multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) for direct air capture (DAC) treats formulation search as unconstrained. We encode the pore-filling boundary as an explicit outcome constraint, c(x) = tanh(1 - phi_hat) - tau, and use it as a diagnostic instrument on a hand-curated, DOI-traceable benchmark of 618 solid-amine formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained MOBO attains higher nominal capacity (3.639 +/- 0.815 vs. 2.964 +/- 0.728 mmol/g, p = 1.0e-11), but across 100 seeds 63.2% of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary versus 39.3% under the constraint: it is rewarded for proposing candidates outside the pore-confined design regime. The constraint steers the front to lower loadings (55.8 vs. 65.2 wt%) and larger pores. The boundary is corroborated once apparatus effects are harmonized hierarchically: 77.8% of kinetic variance is between-laboratory, and pore filling carries a significant kinetic penalty (p = 0.002). Standard hypervolume over-credits feasibility-agnostic methods by 13.9-16.1% (vs. 11.1% constrained), and three surrogate-based analyses---the constrained front, a regeneration-energy third objective, and harmonized kinetics---consistently point to a conservative deployable window at pore filling phi_hat ~ 0.4-0.5 (45-55 wt% loading). The benchmark and associated analysis outputs accompany this submission.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
papers.abstract: The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.

papers.title: Arbitrarily Weak Losses Destroy Fractal Bandstructure in Temporal Fibonacci Quasicrystals
papers.abstract: Lossless photonic crystals with weak refractive index contrasts block limited frequencies. However, the same materials arranged in a non-periodic Fibonacci quasicrystal block all but infinitely rare fractally-distributed frequencies. Similar analysis shows that weak quasiperiodic refractive index variation in time should achieve infinitely broadband gain. We demonstrate that any small experimental losses immediately destroy this effect. Our methods also provide smoothness and approximation theorems for the localisation lengths central to topology in spatial problems.

papers.title: Measuring the Roughness of Quasi-Circular Interfaces at Finite Resolution
papers.abstract: Interface roughness characterizes the boundary fluctuations across different length scales, which can reveal information about a material''s pinning landscape and collective interfacial behaviour. Finite sampling and image resolution can bias the measured scaling properties, however. These effects can particularly complicate comparisons between circular domains of different sizes, where the number of resolved boundary points, and the relationship between angular and physical separations vary with the interface radius. Here, we benchmark the recovery of the roughness exponent and amplitude using synthetic self-affine interfaces generated by Fourier synthesis, mapped onto circular contours, and rasterized onto a pixel grid. We first compare displacement-correlation (B(r)) and structure-factor (S(q)) estimates for different interface lengths. To address non-uniform angular and radial spacing in a circular interface, we assess a reconstruction procedure that weights slope minimization against medial interface position. We find that while spectral estimates were most effective in the original interfaces, this advantage did not persist after circular mapping. Moderate smoothing was found to improve parameter recovery, but stronger smoothing can bias both the scaling exponent and roughness amplitude. These results, verified on both synthetic datasets, and an experimental ferroelectric system, identify limitations of circular-interface roughness measurements and provide a basis for further investigations into the evolution of circular domains under finite resolution experiments.

papers.title: Emergent Chern metal in strongly correlated moiré bilayers
papers.abstract: We investigate the topological properties of a strongly correlated moir\'e transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) bilayer (such as twisted $\mathrm{MoTe}_2$ or $\mathrm{WSe}_2$) hosting a spin-charge separated state coupled to a layer-polarized helical spin texture. Analyzing an effective low-energy Hamiltonian for mobile spinless holons moving through this non-coplanar spinon background, we reveal pronounced asymmetric band warping. This warping closes the global indirect band gap across most of the parameter space, restricting true topological insulators to fine-tuned critical trajectories. However, a finite local direct gap persists, stabilizing broad regions of a topological Chern metal ($C = \pm 1$). Computing the Chern number and density of states, we demonstrate that this phase naturally yields a sizable, non-quantized anomalous Hall response accompanied by finite longitudinal conduction, providing a purely electronic strong-coupling mechanism for dissipative anomalous Hall states in moir\'e systems.

papers.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
papers.abstract: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. Our results establish stacking control as a powerful approach for modulating quantum phases of excitons in 2D semiconductors.
